title: Reusable Agent Learning Loop: Integrate Orchestration, CLI Execution, and Evaluation Across Repositories
target_platform: Companion repo richfrem/agent-plugins-skills (agent-orchestration: orchestrating-agent-work, cli-agent, new shared evaluation skill); Sanctuary thin adapter in sanctuary-core; Protocol 133; APM global + project installs; deterministic fixture tests plus one small genuine CLI run
hypothesis: INTEGRATION CLAIM (engineering, not an empirical research claim): a repository that knows nothing about Sanctuary can run the full loop (work contract with observable acceptance and failure conditions and a budget; lesson retrieval; delegation through cli-agent with code-enforced launch checks; evaluation that returns criterion-level findings; repair of incomplete work; recording of a specific lesson; retrieval and application of that lesson on a second related task; reporting of measured cost with missing data kept unknown) using three shared skills with one authoritative implementation each: orchestrating-agent-work owns the outcome loop, cli-agent enforces execution boundaries and returns structured evidence, and a shared evaluation skill assesses evidence and economics. Sanctuary consumes them through a thin adapter that keeps research manifests, verdicts, Protocol 128 and benchmark definitions local, and records engineering delivery separately from empirical assessment. SCOPE BOUNDARY: this mission does not decide MISSION-053's behavioral claim (baseline-versus-revised orchestrator scenarios) or MISSION-054's Claims A (12 held-out scenarios) and B (12 real work units, longitudinal); both remain explicitly UNASSESSED here. One demonstration is not evidence of long-term savings or autonomy.
falsification_criteria: The integration claim fails if any of these deterministic checks fails on the merged and INSTALLED implementations: (1) two-task fixture in a non-Sanctuary repository: injected execution failure detected by the executor's own checks, repaired and accepted by criterion-level evaluation, a lesson recorded, retrieved before dispatch and applied on the second task (asserted over action traces and state); (2) a task without a rubric works without numeric scores and a configured PR-style rubric works; a high score cannot conceal an unmet required criterion; (3) missing telemetry is reported unknown, never zero; records never leave the configured storage root; (4) the Sanctuary adapter records engineering delivery and empirical assessment separately and engineering acceptance never produces a verdict; (5) existing supported callers of run_agent.py and the Sanctuary eval_gate interface still work; (6) installed copies (Claude, Codex, AGY where configured) equal merged source and a neutral-repo smoke test invokes the installed implementation. Controls not enforced by code are documented as instructions. If the shared evaluator cannot be single-sourced without breaking Sanctuary callers, the limitation is recorded and the mission stays open.
experiment: Inspect both repositories first; reconcile with 053 (guards shipped in PR 748: dispatch_guard.py now owned by cli-agent) and 054 (eval_gate shipped in PR 360: reusable core moves to the companion, Sanctuary keeps a delegating adapter). Build in the companion: executor flags (claim, cwd boundary, timeout, clean-context policy, structured result JSON) wired into run_agent.py; shared evaluation skill (work contract, deterministic criterion checks, validity, proportionate selection, interventions, costs, repairs, lessons with explicit storage root); orchestrator work_loop and references. Build in Sanctuary: adapter translating mission manifests to work contracts and findings to records; documentation in both repositories; PRs and merges; global companion update and local Sanctuary install with installed-interface verification. Budget ceiling set from measured headroom before dispatch; deterministic checks first; at most one small genuine CLI call, labeled apart from mocked tests.
